prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no one “best” platform — pick based on what you need:
  - Airbnb: best for unique stays, lots of host-managed homes, strong host badges (Superhost, Plus), lots of filters.
  - Vrbo: best when you need an entire vacation home (families/groups) — most listings are whole properties and often larger spaces.
  - Booking.com: best for hotels/instant bookings and for last-minute stays or flexible cancellation; also lists apartments and private homes but tends to be hotel-like.

If you tell me your destination, dates, group size and priorities (price, whole home vs private room, family-friendly, work-friendly, pets, flexibility) I can recommend one platform and help search.

How to choose between them (quick guidance)
- Solo traveler / unique local experience / boutique stays: Airbnb.
- Families or big groups who want entire house or condo: Vrbo.
- Need instant confirmation, hotel options, flexible cancellation or last-minute: Booking.com.
- If you care most about price comparison, check all three — often the same property appears on multiple sites with different fees/cancellation rules.

How to find a good host — practical vetting checklist
1. Read recent reviews (last 6–12 months)
   - Look for consistent praise about cleanliness, accuracy, check-in, and host communication.
   - Ignore 1–2 outliers if everything else is good; watch for repeated/recurring complaints.

2. Check host credibility and listing details
   - Badges: Airbnb Superhost/Plus or Vrbo Premier Host are positive signals.
   - Profile: verified ID, complete profile, and many completed stays are good signs.
   - Listing: lots of clear photos, up-to-date calendar, detailed description, and house rules.

3. Look at response metrics
   - High response rate and quick response time in the host profile or listing means they answer questions and handle problems.

4. Inspect the listing carefully
   - Verify exact amenities you need (Wi‑Fi speed, parking, AC/heating, washer, crib, workspace).
   - Check check-in method (self check-in vs key exchange) and arrival instructions.
   - Confirm cleaning fee and any extra charges (security deposit, additional guest fees).

5. Map and neighborhood
   - Use the map view to check proximity to transit/attractions; read recent reviews for noise, safety, and neighborhood convenience.

6. Safety and legality
   - Look for smoke alarms, CO detectors, and clear safety instructions.
   - If applicable, ask whether the host has short-term rental permits or follows local regulations.

7. Ask targeted pre-booking questions (sample message below)
   - “Is the calendar up to date? Are there any house rules I should know about? Is parking included? What’s the Wi‑Fi speed? Where/how will we check in if we arrive late?”
   - Good hosts answer thoroughly and promptly.

8. Watch for red flags
   - Host asks to pay outside the platform.
   - Vague photos, very few reviews, inconsistent messaging, or evasive answers.
   - Multiple recent cancellations or a listing that’s “new” with suspiciously low price.

Sample pre-booking message you can copy/paste
“Hi — I’m [name]. I’m traveling with [number and relation, e.g., 2 adults + 1 child] and arriving on [date], departing [date]. Is the calendar accurate? Is check-in self‑check‑in or will someone meet us? Is there parking included? Can you confirm the Wi‑Fi speed and whether linens and towels are provided? Do you have any house rules we should know about? Thanks!”

Booking & payment safety tips
- Always book and pay through the platform. Never accept offers that ask you to pay by wire transfer, Venmo, or outside the platform — that’s a scam and voids platform protection.
- Read the cancellation policy and refund process before paying.
- Take photos of the place on arrival and report issues to the host and platform within the platform’s timeline if you need a refund.

Extra: when to consider travel insurance
- If your trip is expensive or non-refundable, consider travel insurance that covers cancellations and interruptions, or use a card that includes trip protection.

Quick comparison table (one-line)
- Airbnb: best selection & host community, many unique stays; service fees and strict policies vary.
- Vrbo: best whole-home rentals for families/groups; fewer shared/room options.
- Booking.com: best for hotels/instant bookings and flexible cancellation; big inventory.

If you want, tell me: destination, dates, group size, budget, and top priorities. I’ll recommend one platform and help craft messages or shortlist listings.
